s: snake, a treacherous person (especially a woman)
Schlange.et: From Middle High German slange, from Old High German slango, from Proto-Germanic *slangô. Cognate with German Low German Slang (“snake”), Dutch slang (“snake”), West Frisian slang (“snake”). Compare also Albanian shlligë (“adder”).

s: a municipality of Lippe district, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany

schlank.et: From Middle High German slanc, Middle Low German slank, ultimately related to Proto-Germanic *slingwaną (“to twist, wind”), the source of schlingen.

s: to move in a snakelike manner
Eine Blindschleiche schlängelt sich über den Weg.
to pick one's way, to snake (to move carefully in a winding path around various obstacles)
Er schlängelte sich durch die Menschenmenge.
He picked his way through the crowd.
to snake, to meander, to twist (to follow a curving or winding path; of roads, rails, etc.)
Der Weg schlängelt sich durch den Wald.
The path snakes through the forest.

This is where I saw a snake yesterday.

The dog was devoured by the snake.

She was attacked by a big snake.

I think Tom is afraid of snakes.

He said he was afraid of snakes.

t: Ihr gestreiftes Kleid betont ihre schlanke Figur.
Her stripy dress accentuates her slim figure.
Sie wuchs zu einem schlanken Mädchen auf.
She grew up to be a slim girl.
Maria ist sehr schlank, fast schon mager.
Mary is very slim, almost lean.
Er ist schlank wie ein Wolf.
He is as lean as a wolf.
l: Der Fahrer, ein schlanker Mann mittleren Alters mit Dreitagebart, war allein unterwegs.
Ein schlankes Design ist zudem oft robuster und angenehmer in der Handhabung.

The road wound through the fields.

The path winds through the woods.

A small stream winds its way through the fields.

The footpath winds its way across open fields.
l: Die schlängelt sich um diese Zeit bis an die Flößerbrücke.
